subject: Post-demo recap: selective pseudonymization + shortened log retention proposal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nexamed.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@medbridge.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: selective pseudonymization + shortened log retention proposal

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of asks from Nexa: 
- Prefer 0-retention for PII-containing prompts/outputs for clinical workflows;
- Regional residency: US-only processing and logs;
- Auditability for debugging and safety reviews (replay but limited access).

Redwood proposal (high-level): 
- Selective pseudonymization: we pseudonymize direct identifiers at ingest for a subset of sensitive fields (SSN, MRN, email) while retaining conversational context tokens; pseudonymization keys stored in customer-managed KMS (optional) so reversal requires a customer key.
- Shortened log retention tier: 7-day short logs for pseudonymized sessions + 90-day escrow for encrypted, access-controlled audit snapshots (only available to legal/security teams on exception) — this gives you a near-0 operational window while preserving audit for incidents.
- Residency: we will route all processing and storage to our us-west-2 region and can provide a residency attestation.

Action items and next steps: 
1) Liam/Priya: confirm whether selective pseudonymization (vs full zero-persistence) is acceptable as a technical compromise for production. If yes, tell us which fields you require pseudonymized (we've proposed: name, MRN, email, phone).
2) Redwood (Grace + Alex): we will produce a short design doc and an implementation timeline (attached: selective-pseudonymization-approach-v1.pdf).
3) Legal/Security: we can provide SOC2 artefacts and our data residency attestation. Please confirm the security contacts for Nexa so we can loop them in.

Pricing note: short-log retention (7d) is the default; escrow snapshots (90d) add a modest storage & access fee — I've attached a rough pricing CSV for comparison. We'll refine against your expected throughput once you share call volume.

If that all sounds right, can we schedule a 30m technical touchpoint next week (Grace will lead) to walk the pseudonymization flow and key management options?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Internal takeaways from our side: 

- The product/clinical leads prefer true 0-retention where possible, but they accept a pseudonymization approach if it means we retain no re-identifiable tokens in standard telemetry and if reversal requires our key.
- We need stronger guarantees around access controls for the 90-day escrow snapshots — who signs off, audit trail, and an approval workflow from our compliance team.
- Residency is a must.

Questions / requests before the technical touchpoint: 
1) Is pseudonymization performed client-side (Nexa) or at Redwood ingest? We prefer client-side where possible.
2) Can Redwood provide a short checklist of what the escrow snapshot contains (token-level vs only metadata)?
3) We need an initial SSO + least-privilege admin flow documented so our security engineers can validate.

Priya and I are available Tue/Wed afternoon PT for the 30m session — please send an invite. Also, can you route the security artefacts to our security contact: sec-ops@nexamed.com?

— Liam
Director of Platform Engineering
NexaHealth
